correctness.rationale: Normal functional calculus makes the squared rotated real-part operator norm equal to max of two squared cosine projections. Their difference is a shifted sinusoid -A+B cos(2t-phi), B^2=A^2+U^2; the positive arc |2t-phi|<atan(U/A) integrates exactly to [U-A atan(U/A)]/pi. Direct limits handle U=0, A=0, zero eigenvalues, and one-point spectra. Derivative f_A'(U)=U^2/(A^2+U^2)>0 and radial monotonicity give equality cases; expansion arctan x=x-x^3/3+O(x^5) gives unequal-radius cubic coefficient 4r^3s^3/[3pi(r^2-s^2)^2], versus equal-radius linear cusp. Independent midpoint quadrature at 4096 nodes for 100 random complex pairs agreed to max absolute error 1.005e-6; this corroborates rather than proves the all-Hilbert-space statement.
residual_risks: No classification for spectra with 3 or more values, or nonnormal operators; no general perturbation stability claim.
